4th Period.workingNow: Embedding your ROLLER game on your portfolio site and finishing your design document.
4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: One design document in your portfolio repo bringing together your mechanics, dynamics, aesthetic and state map — plus your ROLLER game embedded and playable on your portfolio site — pushed by Sunday night.
4th Period.smartGoal: I can embed my game on my portfolio site so that anyone can play it right next to the design document that explains it.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.16 — Incorporate existing code, media, and libraries into original programs, and give attribution.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.2 — Interacting with others in written English in various communicative forms.
agenda: I do: embed ROLLER on your portfolio site (12 min)
We do: check one portfolio against the rubric (7 min)
You do: embed, then finish your document (23 min)
Exit Ticket: paste your live portfolio link (3 min)
4th Period.connections: Your design document explains a game nobody can play yet. Today you fix that — the base game goes live on your portfolio site, embedded right above the design that says what you are going to do to it. Next week you start building, and every change will show up on that page.

6th Period.workingNow: Handing your diagram to a partner and watching them try to get it stuck.
6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: A finished state machine diagram for one thing you choose — at least 5 states, every state with a labeled way in and a labeled way out — partner-tested and turned in by Sunday night.
6th Period.smartGoal: I can test my state machine with a partner so that I can find the paths I did not think about.
6th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.15 — Seek and incorporate feedback from team members and users to refine a solution that meets user needs.
6th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.11 — Justifying own arguments and evaluating others' arguments in speaking and writing.
agenda: Overview: today you test it (2 min)
I do: how to walk a partner through a machine (8 min)
We do: trace one path as a class (7 min)
You do: partner test, then fix your diagram (25 min)
Exit Ticket: one thing you fixed (5 min)
6th Period.connections: You have five states on paper. Today someone else drives — they pick triggers and you move through your own machine until something breaks. Fix it, and you have a finished state machine. Next week you use it to build a real game with SchoolAI.
